articles.title: Trump announces diesel deal with Russia in bid to lower prices
Polttoaineet | Zelenskyi: Trumpin ja Putinin diesel-diili on ”heikko päätös”

econ.reason: The Washington Post frames the deal as a move to lower prices and presents it as a market-supply decision; Helsingin Sanomat is mostly a neutral report of a temporary permit for Russian diesel.

social.reason: The Washington Post stresses alignment with Russia and opposition to Ukraine’s attacks on refineries, which leans toward a national-security/order frame; Helsingin Sanomat mainly quotes Zelensky criticizing the deal and does not add a broader ideological frame.

articles.title: Justice Department investigating major TV networks over suspending pool coverage of Trump
DOJ investigating TV networks over suspension of press pool after Trump media ban

econ.reason: Both articles center on an antitrust investigation, but NBC News frames it mainly as a press-freedom clash and calls it intimidation, while CBS News more neutrally explains the Sherman Act and competition law.

social.reason: Both are strongly about media access and First Amendment rights; NBC News is more explicitly supportive of journalists’ independence and condemns the probe as intimidation, while CBS News is still critical of Trump but more procedural.

articles.title: Trump rips into Volodymyr Zelensky — insisting it’s time for Ukraine to ‘get a new president’
Kiev respalda a Zelenski y considera que las palabras de Trump "confirman que lo está haciendo bien"

econ.reason: New York Post emphasizes lowering diesel prices, helping farmers/consumers, and a market-supply deal; 20minutos is mostly about sanctions and wartime diplomacy, without a clear market-vs-regulation framing.

social.reason: New York Post centers Trump’s hard line on Zelensky and calls for a new Ukrainian president, while 20minutos stresses Ukraine’s right to choose its leader and frames the war in terms of independence, freedom, and dignity.

articles.title: Trump: – På tide for Ukraina å få ny president
Trump Suggests Ukraine Remove Zelensky and Replace Him With Leader 'Who Can Make a Deal'

econ.reason: TV 2 frames the diesel deal mainly as a political giveaway that could hurt Ukraine and consumers; Breitbart frames it as supplying the ‘American and Global Marketplace’ and emphasizes market flow.

social.reason: TV 2 stresses that Russia is the aggressor and counters Trump’s attack on Zelensky; Breitbart highlights Zelensky’s failed elections, ‘dictator’ label, and the need for a leader ‘who can make a deal’.

articles.title: Trump calls for Ukraine to replace Zelenskyy after clash over Russia diesel deal: 'Get a new president'
Trump tordner mod Zelenskyj: Ukraine har brug for en ny præsident

econ.reason: Fox News stresses easing sanctions and boosting fuel supplies/pump prices, while Jyllands-Posten foregrounds criticism of the diesel deal, support for sanctions, and limits on Russia’s war financing.

social.reason: Fox News is mostly a straight report on the dispute, while Jyllands-Posten adds Zelenskyy’s criticism, European support for him, and the Russian strike that killed civilians, giving it a more sympathetic pro-Ukraine tone.

articles.title: Trump: Ukrainan on aika saada uusi presidentti
Donald Trump affirme "qu'il est temps pour l'Ukraine d'avoir un nouveau président" pour parvenir "à un accord" avec la Russie

econ.reason: Ilta-Sanomat only states that Trump says Ukraine needs a new president; franceinfo adds that this is about making “an accord” with Russia and highlights diesel shortages, giving it a more transaction-and-economy framing.

social.reason: Ilta-Sanomat is a plain headline, while franceinfo stresses Zelensky’s responsibility and the need for a new president to reach a deal, which frames the story more around order and leadership change.

articles.title: Ukraine: Donald Trump fordert Machtwechsel in Kiew nach Diesel-Streit
Trump contro Zelensky: "L'Ucraina vada al voto, Putin vuole l'intesa". raid russi sul Dnipropetrovsk

econ.reason: Der Spiegel centers Trump’s diesel deal, sanctions rollback, and fuel-price concerns in a way that is more market/fiscal-reserve oriented; RaiNews stresses keeping sanctions, pressuring Russia, and condemns the deal as helping Putin.

social.reason: Both are pro-Ukraine and anti-Russian, but RaiNews more strongly frames Zelensky’s legitimacy, sovereignty, and European solidarity against aggression, while Der Spiegel is more straightforwardly reported with less normative emphasis.

articles.title:
Il bluff di Putin sul diesel: le raffinerie dello Zar

in ginocchio dopo gli attacchi
Donald Trump made Russian diesel deal with Vladimir Putin after row with Volodymyr Zelensky

econ.reason: GB News emphasizes lifting sanctions and increasing diesel supply to bring prices down, while La Stampa is mainly a critical description of Russia’s export losses with no clear policy preference.

social.reason: GB News foregrounds Zelensky’s criticism, civilian deaths, and condemnation of Russian attacks, while La Stampa only briefly attacks Putin without broader social or rights framing.

articles.title: Un conflicto nuclear y el uso malicioso de la inteligencia artificial se cuelan entre las amenazas para la salud mundial: “Sería un apocalipsis”
Nuclear war and malicious use of AI threaten end of humanity by 2100, says Lancet assessment

econ.reason: The Guardian explicitly includes “cuts to aid spending by wealthy countries” as one of the threats, while El País sticks to the health-risk list without any fiscal or spending angle.

social.reason: Both articles frame the issue as global catastrophic risks from nuclear war and AI, with no notable emphasis on identity, religion, immigration, or other social-policy themes.

articles.title: Erie gunman killed eight including pregnant woman and two children before barricading himself inside home in SWAT standoff as police say rampage is 'most heartbreaking scene they've ever encountered'
Ni drept etter masseskyting i Pennsylvania

econ.reason: Neither article frames the event in economic terms such as taxes, spending, regulation, or welfare.

social.reason: Daily Mail emphasizes violent crime, SWAT standoff, and police reaction, giving it a more law-and-order/security frame; NRK stays more factual and restrained, with less emotive emphasis.
